summary: Add a NOT VALID foreign‑key constraint on account_user.referrer_id, backfill rows that reference non‑existent users to NULL, deploy the new version with a state‑only migration, retire the old version, then validate the FK constraint so both versions can safely write the column after the migration.
write_consistency: During the overlap the old version continues to write referrer_id as an integer; the NOT VALID FK permits this without immediate validation. A backfill step cleans any orphan references to NULL while both versions are live. After the old version is retired the FK is validated, guaranteeing that subsequent writes from the new version (which expects a FK) respect the reference.

stages.description: Add foreign key constraint NOT VALID on referrer_id
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD CONSTRAINT fk_referrer FOREIGN KEY (referrer_id) REFERENCES account_user(id) NOT VALID;

stages.description: Set referrer_id to NULL for rows that reference non‑existent users
sql: UPDATE account_user SET referrer_id = NULL WHERE referrer_id IS NOT NULL AND referrer_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM account_user);
ALTER TABLE account_user VALIDATE CONSTRAINT fk_referrer;
